Experience with observability tools (e.g., log aggregation, dashboards, alert tuning) and performance monitoring. Background supporting regulated environments with audit and compliance considerations. Why Join Join a supportive team focused on delivering stable systems and great end-user experiences. Develop practical expertise in system reliability, integrations, and operational best practices for the insurance and accounting domain. Build valuable skills in troubleshooting, automation, documentation, and cross-team collaboration. Make a meaningful impact by improving system performance, reliability, and data accuracy for critical business workflows. review_candidates.title: Network Administrator
review_candidates.description: Network Administrator RJ45, SFP+, QSFP, IP, BGP, TCP, UDP, TLS, DHCP, SFTP, F5... Pokud to pro tebe není jen shluk náhodných znaků, ale vidíš za tím živou infrastrukturu, zbystři. Hledáme parťáka, který má síťařinu v krvi, rád řeší komplexní technické výzvy a chce rozšířit tým lidí, kteří IT doslova žijí. Tato pozice není o rutinním klikání – naše síť je živý, různorodý organismus plný moderních technologií a její správa vyžaduje maximální zodpovědnost. Co budeš dělat? Komplexní správa a rozvoj: Kompletní péče o naši síťovou infrastrukturu od návrhu až po realizaci. Architektura a inovace: Nebudeš jen udržovat status quo – čeká tě implementace nových technologií a aktivní vyhledávání cest k optimalizaci a modernizaci sítě. Instalace a konfigurace: Hardwaru i softwaru (u nás si sáhneš na spoustu různých technologií). Troubleshooting: Diagnostika a řešení složitých síťových incidentů, které vyžadují analytické myšlení a rychlé jednání. Podpora: Řešení pokročilých požadavků od našich zákazníků i kolegů. Co od tebe očekáváme? Vysokou míru zodpovědnosti a pečlivosti: Výpadky sítě bolí. Hledáme člověka, který domýšlí věci do důsledku, nezkracuje si cestu a na jehož práci je 100% spolehnutí. Zápal a chuť se samovzdělávat: Technologie letí dopředu a náš stack je pestrý. Klíčový je pro nás tvůj vnitřní drive – musíš se chtít učit nové věci sám od sebe, sledovat trendy a neustále se v oboru rozvíjet. Solidní základ: Znalosti v oblasti správy sítí, routovacích/switchingových protokolů a základní administraci OS Linux. Vzdělání: VŠ nebo SŠ technického zaměření (CISCO akademie je velkou výhodou). Komunikativnost a týmovost: Nebát se mluvit se zákazníkem i kolegy, umět věci vysvětlit, ptát se. Flexibilitu: Občasné držení pohotovosti (L2, střídáme se fér v rámci týmu). Co u nás získáš? Zázemí stabilní, ryze české společnosti s dlouholetou historií. Pružnou pracovní dobu: Fixní čas máme od 9:00 do 15:00, zbytek si plánuješ podle sebe. 5 týdnů dovolené. Finanční ohodnocení, které odpovídá náročnosti pozice + podílové odměny. Uvolněnou a přátelskou atmosféru. Všichni si tykáme, pomáháme si a chápeme, že každý má někdy den blbec.

review_candidates.title: Information and Communications Technology (ICT) Officer (P)
review_candidates.description: Job Description Introduction Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental, and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants. IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive, and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration . Applications are welcome from first- and second-tier candidates, particularly qualified female candidates as well as applications from the non-represented member countries of IOM. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, the following are considered first-tier candidates: Internal candidates Candidates from the following IOM Member States that are not represented among staff members in the Professional and higher categories: Bahamas, Barbados, Cabo Verde, Comoros, Congo (the), Cook Islands, Dominica, Federated States of Micronesia, Grenada, Guinea-Bissau, Holy See, Iceland, Israel, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Namibia, Nauru, Palau, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Samoa, Sao Tome and Principe, Seychelles, Solomon Islands, Suriname, Timor-Leste, Tonga, Trinidad and Tobago, Tuvalu, Vanuatu Second Tier Candidates Include All external candidates, except candidates from non-represented member states of IOM. Organizational Context and Scope Under the overall supervision of Chief of Mission (CoM), direct supervision of the Head of Resources Management and in close coordination with relevant staff from ICT department counterparts in the Regional Officer Asia and Pacific (ROAP) and the Department of Information and Communications Technology at HQ, the Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Officer will supervise and coordinate the ICT operations in the Country Office (CO) including its Sub-Offices. Responsibilities Supervise and coordinate the activities of the Information and Communications Technology (ICT) Unit in the Country Office by ensuring that all requirements are addressed in a timely and accurately, with an efficient allocation of resources, and that all operations are in compliance with IOM ICT policies and standards and are in line with the ICT strategy. Coordinate the continuous engagement and liaison with the CO’s management, Heads of units and field operations, for the adequate and timely provision of ICT solutions and services to satisfy operational needs, including emergencies as necessary. Act as the ICT business relationship and cybersecurity local liaison Focal Point with counterparts such as IOM programmes, global cybersecurity programme, Governmental, donors, United Nations Agencies, Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs), ICT service providers, and Vendors for coordinated and adequate provision of ICT services, digital innovation, technologies and supplies. Participate in the ICT Working Group in the country, representing the CO in discussions and initiatives. Provide technical support for the CO’s ICT services and supervise, train, and equip the CO’s ICT Team to effectively implement strategic initiatives, timely respond to information security incidents, and provide Tier 1 support and escalate to the relevant specialist teams/units, when needed, for immediate corrective/remedial actions. Contribute to the preparation of the CO’s ICT documentation including office-specific Standard Operating Procedures (SOP), Business Continuity Plan, Disaster Recovery Plans and ICT Risk record for the CO’s ICT-related services. Coordinate and monitor the delivery and efficiency of services and redundancy in line with IOM ICT standards while checking that global ICT SOPs are complied with. Contribute to the service improvement assessments and provide recommendations to the CO’s management to optimize and implement ICT Infrastructure and solutions to ensure the efficient functioning of CO’s operations. Maintain and check that all technical specifications for procurement and provision of ICT-related equipment, supplies, services, and technical evaluations are in line with ICT standards and policies, and are adequately managed. Liaise with CO’s Supply Chain Unit to guide on proper provision of ICT-related equipment, supplies, services, and propose the most suitable solutions. In coordination with the ICT Information Security Unit at HQ, act as the Focal Point, the first line of cybersecurity defense, and first local cybersecurity incident responder in the CO. Facilitate the implementation of security and compliance controls of the IOM global cybersecurity programme and compliance with the IOM global cybersecurity, and other compliances required by the donors, operational frameworks and standards. Perform such other duties as may be assigned. Qualifications Required Qualifications and Experience Education Master’s degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Information Management, Information Technology, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with two years of relevant professional experience; or, University degree in the above fields with four years of relevant professional experience. Certificate in any of the following: Cisco Certified Network Associate (CCNA), Microsoft Azure certifications, Microsoft Certified System Administrator (MCSA), Microsoft Certified Database Administrator (MCDBA), Microsoft Certified System Engineer (MCSE) is a distinct advantage. review_candidates.title: UN WOMEN: Regional Gender Statistics Specialist - Cairo, Egypt - FTA - P4
review_candidates.description: Job Description Background: UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace and security. UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace, and security. To support member states in implementing the 2030 Agenda, the UN Women’s Global Flagship Programme Initiative (FPI) “Making Every Woman and Girl Count” (Women Count) aims to effect a radical shift in the availability, accessibility, and use of data and statistics on key aspects of gender equality and women’s empowerment. The FPI envisions a multi-year and multi-country programme of work, complemented by global and regional strategies linking normative and technical work on gender statistics at the global level to the regional and national levels through three interlinked areas of work: Building a supportive policy and institutional environment for the localization and effective monitoring of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs); Increasing the quality, comparability, and regularity of gender statistics to address national data gaps and meet reporting commitments under the SDGs; and Ensuring that gender statistics are accessible to users in governments, civil society, academia, and the private sector, to strengthen adequate demand for their production. In line with this global FPI developed by UN Women HQ, UN Women Arab States Regional Office developed a regional project that is specific to the context of the Arab States region and responds to the Regional Strategic Note 2026-29 in order to: Advance the production and use of gender statistics across the region and strengthen national-level SDGs monitoring and reporting through building holistic systems at national and regional level to measure SDG 5 and other key SDG indicators that require sex-disaggregation; and Collaborate with regional bodies/partners in the Arab States to produce comprehensive and comparative gender statistics, analysis and advance accessibility and knowledge sharing. Under the direct supervision of the Deputy Regional Director of UN Women ROAS and matrix supervision of the Chief of the Research and Data Section of UN Women HQ, the Regional Specialist on Gender Statistics and SDG Monitoring will oversee the regional implementation of Women Count; provide technical leadership, knowledge and capacity development services to regional and national partners, UN Women offices and project/programme teams to advance capacities, knowledge sharing and data availability in the area of gender statistics and SDGs monitoring; advise and support the regions senior leadership team on UN Women’s strategic engagement at the regional and country level, including by building partnerships and advocating for better gender data; and leading knowledge generation in the area of gender statistics and SDGs monitoring and implementation. Key Functions and Accountabilities: Manage and oversee the implementation of Making Every Woman and Girl Count (Women Count) at the regional level Lead the planning of the regional project and activities to ensure timely and comprehensive implementation of Women Count and ensure that the implementation of Women Count follows strict quality standards, as established under the Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics and the Principles Governing International Statistical Activities; Lead the alignment of the regional project to the Regional Strategic Note (2026-29) and ensure alignment with national priorities as defined in the UNSDCFs and UN Women Country level Strategic Notes; Working with the HQ Programme Management Specialist, manage and oversee programmatic and administrative management necessary for the implementation of Women Count in the Arab States, including budget planning, budget/programme performance oversight, and inputs to results-based budgeting; Oversee regional project monitoring reports on Strategic Note and Strategic Plan indicators as related to the Women Count project; Coordinate with the team at Headquarters to report on activities, contribute to the regional perspective and ensure that the implementation of regional activities is in line with the overall objectives of Women Count; Ensure that the organization’s resources are being spent efficiently, in accordance with its objectives; Working with the team at HQ, provide substantive technical inputs to the production of quality monitoring and evaluation plans that are in line with and consistent with the overall objectives of the project and UN Women’s regional strategic note; Oversee the collection, analysis, and reporting of programme data and results in coordination with the HQ Programme Management Specialist and the Monitoring, Learning and Evaluation (MLE) Specialist; Effectively manage the targets established and oversee the monitoring of results, including ensuring adequate inputs and performance indicators are incorporated to allow for effective progress monitoring and successful achievement of Women Count; Contribute to all activities related to the learning, monitoring, and evaluation of Women Count and support regional monitoring related to the UN Women Strategic Plan 2026-2029, particularly Outcome 2, and the Regional Strategic Note. Establish and provide targeted strategic knowledge and capacity development services to UN Women offices and project/programme teams in alignment with regional and national level Strategic Notes, and build capacity to strengthen policy and institutional capacities, quality data production and use Lead the establishment of UN Women’s statistical strategy and its implementation in the region, including focused strategic direction and positioning of UN Women’s work on gender and statistics at the regional and country levels in the period of the regional Strategic note (2026-29); Provide direct technical and advisory support to UN Women’s MEWGC pathfinder and non-pathfinder countries in the region; Produce and disseminate templates, guidance notes, and methodologies, including for conducting country-level assessments, and national and sectoral plans to monitor the gender-related commitments in the SDGs and data use plans; Provide adequate technical and policy leadership to UN Women offices and ROAS Member States on demand, including providing direct technical support to countries on all matters related to gender statistics and SDGs monitoring; Provide referral services to countries, including as necessary, through the establishment of a roster of thematic consultants and experts on gender statistics; Produce and disseminate technical notes and methodologies for Tier I and Tier II SDG indicators, based on needs, capacities, and expertise; Lead and oversee regional capacity building initiatives for UN Women country and programme offices in order to progressively strengthen their capacity in the area of gender statistics; Establish and actively lead a regional community of practice to facilitate knowledge sharing, improve coordination, and support knowledge sharing on gender statistics. Codify best practices and lessons learned, and knowledge-sharing, covering all aspects of the regional programme; Lead and manage UN Women’s strategic engagement at the regional level, including building partnerships, providing technical support and advancing gender data Develop and manage the partnerships needed to implement regional FPI, including with governments, donors, international agencies, civil society and philanthropic organizations, and the private sector; Strengthen UN Women’s relationship with key regional players such as ESCWA Division of Statistics, League of Arab States (LAS) statistics unit, Arab Institute for Training and Research in Statistics (AITRS), OIC statistical economic and social research and training center for Islamic countries, UNECA, and other international agencies, academic research institutes, and civil society organizations, particularly to strengthen gender data use in the region; Facilitate South-South and triangular cooperation to support sub-regional and national processes on gender statistics; Advance discussions around the regional adaptation of SDGs indicators, including by promoting a strong link between globally agreed indicators and their regional adaptations and ensuring that these are fed into national plans to localize SDGs; Identify and implement opportunities to deepen the work on gender statistics with the UN’s Regional Collaboration Platforms Issue-Based Coalition (IBC), particularly the IBC on Gender; Lead and quality assure UN-Women regional technical contributions to global/ regional/sub-regional/national workshops, seminars, colloquia, and other training events related to statistics and SDGs monitoring and implementation, including proposals concerning agenda topics, possible participants, preparation of documents and presentations, etc.; Promote and publicize the work of UN Women on gender statistics; Lead resource mobilization by advising senior leadership in the region and HQ women count team, working with regional strategic partnership specialist, developing concept notes and prodocs and engaging with partners and potential donors to raise additional funding for the MEWGC project; Lead capacity development initiatives, including the delivery of specialized technical training to support the implementation of the regional strategic note; Advance inter-regional knowledge on best practices in data collection, particularly with respect to the production of gender statistics; Lead the monitoring and collection of use cases of gender statistics at the regional level; Produce regional guidance notes on best practices and lessons learned in gender statistics; Advance normative frameworks to create and enabling environment for the collection and use of gender statistics. The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organisation. Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: The incumbent leads a team of 6, which includes 2 direct reports (NOB & GS ) including matrix manager for 4 country office staff (NOC & GS l) and affiliate personnel (consultants). Competencies : Core Values: Integrity; Professionalism; Respect for Diversity. Core Competencies: Awareness and Sensitivity Regarding Gender Issues; Accountability; Creative Problem Solving; Effective Communication; Inclusive Collaboration; Stakeholder Engagement; Leading by Example. Please visit this link for more information on UN Women’s Values and Competencies Framework: Functional Competencies: Excellent knowledge related to current policies and practices in the area of gender statistics; Strong knowledge of modalities of UN technical support at global, regional, and country levels, with a focus on gender statistics; Strong leadership skills and ability to lead by example and motivate a diverse team to achieve results in a timely manner; Strong knowledge of UN intergovernmental processes, including the monitoring framework established for SDGs; Strong communications skills, with proven expertise in writing cogent and convincing policy and programme documents for development practitioners; Proven analytical and problem-solving skills; Ability to leverage information technology, information systems, management techniques, and tools for optimal office performance; Strong planning, goal-setting, and prioritization skills; Ability to establish and foster good relations with government counterparts, UN agencies, donors, and NGO partners; Proven ability to promote individual and organizational learning and knowledge sharing using formal and informal methodologies; Proven ability to organize and manage knowledge management processes and tools; Excellent presentational and public speaking skills. Required Qualifications: Education and Certification: Master’s degree or equivalent in statistics, demography, economics, is required; A first-level university degree in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Experience: At least 7 years of progressively responsible work experience in gender statistics is required; Experience in gender equality and women's empowerment programming is required; Experience working in the UN system is desirable; Experience in leading and managing personnel in international settings is required; Experience in the usage of computers and office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.) and spreadsheet and database packages; experience in handling web-based management systems is required; Experience in the use of a modern web-based ERP System, preferably Oracle Cloud, AI, is desirable; Experience working in the Arab States region is desirable. Languages: Fluency in English is required; Knowledge of another official UN language (French, Arabic) is desirable. Statements : In July 2010, the United Nations General Assembly created UN Women, the United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women. The creation of UN Women came about as part of the UN reform agenda, bringing together resources and mandates for greater impact. It merges and builds on the important work of four previously distinct parts of the UN system (DAW, OSAGI, INSTRAW and UNIFEM), which focused exclusively on gender equality and women's empowerment. review_candidates.description: Your mission Your mission Are you energized by speaking with people, uncovering opportunities, and opening doors? Do you thrive in a fast-paced sales environment where every conversation has the potential to create value? As a Tele Sales Representative (m/f/d)) at myneva, you will play a critical role in our sales organisation by engaging with prospective customers across the German market. Working closely with Marketing and our Account Executives, you will primarily qualify Marketing Qualified Leads (MQLs) and inbound enquiries, ensuring they are sales-ready before handing them over to the sales team. Alongside lead qualification, you will also undertake targeted outbound prospecting to engage high-potential accounts and generate additional pipeline. This is an excellent opportunity for an ambitious sales professional who enjoys building relationships, is motivated by achieving targets. What you will do: Respond quickly to Marketing Qualified Leads (MQLs) and inbound enquiries, engaging prospects while interest is high. Qualify prospects through discovery conversations to understand their needs, challenges, buying process, and fit. Schedule high-quality sales meetings and ensure a seamless handover to the appropriate Account Executive. Conduct targeted outbound prospecting into agreed accounts to create additional pipeline opportunities. Build rapport quickly with decision-makers and confidently lead conversations. Handle objections professionally and uncover customer pain points without relying on a script. Maintain accurate records of all activities, conversations, and opportunities in HubSpot CRM. Collaborate closely with Marketing and Sales to maximise lead conversion and continuously improve lead quality. Consistently achieve pipeline generation, meeting, and qualification targets. Your profile 2–4 years of experience in a Tele Sales Representative or Sales Development Representative (SDR) role within a B2B SaaS business. A proven track record of consistently achieving or exceeding pipeline generation and meeting targets, with measurable results you can demonstrate. Strong outbound calling skills with the ability to guide conversations, ask insightful questions, and confidently overcome objections. High energy, positive attitude, and a genuine enjoyment of engaging with people. Business-fluent German and good English communication skills. Self-motivated, coachable, and resilient—you actively seek feedback, learn quickly, and stay motivated through rejection. Comfortable using modern sales technology, including HubSpot CRM, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, sales engagement platforms, and data enrichment tools. Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple leads and priorities effectively. Why us? We offer a competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package. Our employees benefit from extensive occupational healthcare and health insurance. A lunch benefit is also available to support your everyday well-being. In addition, we offer exercise, cultural, and massage benefits. Flexible working hours and remote work options provide a good work-life balance. You will be part of a supportive and collaborative international team environment. Continuous learning and development programs offer opportunities for personal and professional growth. Regular team events and activities contribute to our engaging and welcoming company culture. contact information If this sounds like you, we look forward to receiving your detailed application materials—including your salary expectations and your earliest possible start date—via our online application form! About Us Welcome to myneva - together, we shape digital care. myneva is one of the leading European software providers for the social sector. Our solutions focus on shaping the world around our clients and their needs. By digitising processes, we help care givers gain more time to support their clients, enabling them to enjoy a better quality of life. As an ambitious team, we are pursuing increasing internationalisation and a clear mission to become #1 in Europe.

Sinds 2016 zijn we hard gegroeid naar een organisatie met enkele honderden medewerkers buiten in de uitvoering en ongeveer 25 collega's op kantoor. Ondanks onze sterke groei is de vertrouwde familiecultuur het kloppende hart van onze organisatie. Bij ons ben je geen nummer, maar een gewaardeerde vakman. We bouwen op elkaars expertise, de deuren staan altijd open en successen vieren we samen. In ons werk staan kwaliteit, veiligheid en duurzaamheid voorop, maar minstens zo belangrijk is de manier waarop we met elkaar omgaan: betrokken, respectvol en rechtvaardig. Interesse? review_candidates.description: Job Description Introduction Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental, and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants. IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive, and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration . Applications are welcome from first- and second-tier candidates, particularly qualified female candidates as well as applications from the non-represented member countries of IOM. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, the following are considered first-tier candidates: Internal candidates Candidates from the following IOM Member States that are not represented among staff members in the Professional and higher categories: Bahamas, Barbados, Cabo Verde, Comoros, Congo (the), Cook Islands, Dominica, Federated States of Micronesia, Grenada, Guinea-Bissau, Holy See, Iceland, Israel, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Namibia, Nauru, Palau, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Samoa, Sao Tome and Principe, Seychelles, Solomon Islands, Suriname, Timor-Leste, Tonga, Trinidad and Tobago, Tuvalu, Vanuatu Second Tier Candidates Include All external candidates, except candidates from non-represented member states of IOM. Organizational Context and Scope Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission (CoM) and direct supervision of the Deputy Chief of Mission (DCoM), in coordination with the Programme Managers, Senior Resource Management Officer, Heads of Sub-Offices IOM West and Central of Africa Regional Office (RO) and IOM’s Headquarters (HQ), the Head of Programme Coordination and Innovation Unit (PCIU) will be responsible for the management and coordination of unit activities, including programme and project conceptualization, proposal development, Monitoring and Evaluation, support the Country Office (CO) strategic planning and relationships with UN, donors and the Government of Nigeria, particularly in relation to the operational aspects of programmes/projects and resource mobilization. Responsibilities Manage and supervise the staff of the Mission Support and Innovation Unit, ensuring their effective and timely performance of development, implementation, and reporting tasks for IOM Nigeria’s programmes/projects according to institutional guidance. Assess potential project and funding opportunities, prepare project proposals and concept notes in the areas of interest to IOM Nigeria, and review and improve project reports, fact sheets and other documents in coordination with relevant Programme/Project managers and programme units. Support the coordination and evaluation of programme and project activities of IOM Nigeria to ensure timely and effective implementation and quality reporting and advise the DCoM of the corrective measures that may be needed. Support liaison with donors, project partners, other IOM Country Offices, RO, and HQ to facilitate coordinated project implementation and synergies and to make recommendations on donor/partner engagement. Provide advice for the mainstreaming of relevant African Union, Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), West African Community, Intergovernmental Authority on Development and Common Market for West Africa policies and frameworks into internal frameworks, policies, as well as national-level programming and design. Keep abreast of and analyse migration issues, policies, and emerging trends, identify priorities, and recommend actions to the Deputy Chief of Mission in relation to risks and opportunities for IOM. Identify priorities, challenges and issues to be addressed within the country office as appropriate and propose corrective actions. Provide support and guidance to Programme/Project Managers and other project staff on programme/project implementation, monitoring and evaluation, and quality assurance. Participate in relevant UN and inter-agency meetings and mechanisms to facilitate the integration of IOM programmes into inter-agency processes and the mainstreaming of migration into Common Country Analysis and Cooperation frameworks. Support IOM Nigeria in working with respective national counterparts to facilitate cooperation, external relations, and liaison activities. In close coordination with the Information Management System Officer, provide evidence-based information on IOM Nigeria’s project development and fundraising efforts through targeted assessment surveys, analyses, studies, and systematic publication. Develop and disseminate communications and visibility materials, such as quarterly reports, newsletters, flash reports, etc., and respond to information requests from HQ and Regional Office. Facilitate the generation and use of knowledge to promote improved policy engagement, project development and management in Nigeria and the West and Central Africa region. Perform such other duties as may be assigned. Qualifications Required Qualifications and Experience Education Master’s degree in Political or Social Science, International Relations, Law, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with five years of relevant professional experience; or, University degree in the above fields with seven years of relevant professional experience. Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database. Experience Experience in the field of international migration, management, and evaluation; Work experience in the field of migration issues, including operational and field experience, IOM Project Development, Management, Implementation and Monitoring systems; Experience in dealing with donors on project implementation and reporting; Experience and excellent understanding of the migration themes in West Africa and extensive knowledge of the arid and semi-arid regions; and, Experience in liaising with governmental authorities, other national/international institutions, and Non-Governmental Organizations. Skills Knowledge in project monitoring and evaluation is required; Demonstrated expertise in thematic areas relevant to project liaison, reporting, and monitoring; and, Knowledge and experience of regional issues is an advantage. Languages For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written). Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage. Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments. Required Competencies IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link . Competencies will be assessed during the selection process. Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values: Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion. Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct. Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges. Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance. Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated. Core Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2 Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results. Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action-oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes. Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate. Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work. Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way. Managerial Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2 Leadership: Provides a clear sense of direction, leads by example and demonstrates the ability to carry out the Organization’s vision. Assists others to realize and develop their leadership and professional potential. Empowering others: Creates an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential. Building Trust: Promotes shared values and creates an atmosphere of trust and honesty. Strategic thinking and vision: Works strategically to realize the Organization’s goals and communicates a clear strategic direction. Humility: Leads with humility and shows openness to acknowledging own shortcomings. Notes Internationally recruited professional staff are required to be mobile. Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category. Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation. This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months. Appointment will be subject to all clearances, including medical and security, as well as accreditation, and any residency or visa requirements. Vacancies close at 23:59 local time in Geneva, Switzerland, on the respective closing date. No late applications will be accepted. IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, harassment, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and any forms of discrimination. IOM is committed to promote the protection and safeguarding of all children. IOM conducts reference checks and background verification, including through system-wide databases such as ClearCheck, to help ensure that candidates have no record of misconduct, including on sexual harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, or fraud. Candidates are expected to uphold these standards and principles at all times. IOM does not charge any fees at any stage of the recruitment process—whether for application, interview, processing, training, or otherwise—and does not request any information related to bank accounts. IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM WAVE system (for internal candidates, link here ). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies.

review_candidates.description: Job Description Background: UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace and security. Through its regional thematic policy advisers, the UN Women West and Central Africa Regional Office (WCARO), based in Dakar, Senegal, works to provide strategic guidance and support for mandate implementation to UN Women country offices and programmes. Policy Advisors/Specialists analyze regional trends and emerging issues related to promoting women’s rights and gender equality in West and Central Africa; facilitate UN regional-level coordination activities and partnership-building with regional organizations; and oversee knowledge production and knowledge management to inform advocacy and policy strategic direction. Under the supervision of the Deputy Regional Director and in close consultation with Ending Violence against Women and other relevant Sections in HQ, the Ending Violence against Women Policy Specialist will oversee and provide high-level technical advice and support to the UN Women country and regional offices working on different areas of Ending Violence against Women programming. The Policy Specialist will provide capacity building to Country Offices (CO), establish and strengthen partnerships, facilitate internal coordination within the relevant divisions of UN Women to ensure delivery of programme results and implementation of policy guidance in Ending Violence against Women programming and link the Ending Violence against Women work of UN-Women with the broader UN reform. They will coordinate UN Women WCARO’s engagement in and implementation of specific initiatives such as Spotlight. The Policy Specialist supervises and leads the Ending Violence against Women unit staff. Key Functions and Accountabilities : Manage the development of programmes on Ending Violences Against Women to Country Office teams Manage the development and implementation of an integrated strategy for the delivery of technical assistance, policy advocacy and programme support in the region; Manage the development of regional programme documents on Ending Violence against Women Oversee the contextualization/ localization of programme documents, country strategies, and knowledge products, and ensure proper monitoring and reporting in Ending Violence against Women. Lead the provision of capacity-building support to Country Office teams and partners Lead country office and multi-country office programme teams in developing and strengthening policies, projects/ programmes and modalities to support the implementation of global norms and standards; and ensuring proper monitoring; Manage the identification of knowledge and implementation gaps and possible solutions; Develop, implement and monitor capacity building initiatives; Lead the provision of technical policy advice to programme/ project managers/ specialists in the CO. Establish and strengthen strategic partnerships with stakeholders, regional/ international actors and development partners Build and strengthen strategic partnerships for the advancement of Ending Violence against Women; Build and strengthen close liaisons with relevant donors and other actors supporting efforts towards Ending Violence against Women]; Produce periodic updates and briefs on regional/country development situations to be used by stakeholders, CO and HQ; Maintain close contact with relevant staff in UN Women HQ. Manage the resource mobilization strategy for Ending Violence against Women in the region Participate in the implementation, monitoring and periodic updating of the resource mobilization strategy on Ending Violence against Women in the region; Provide technical support to field- based presences in the region in mobilizing resources for the implementation of Ending Violence against Women Research and analyze information on donors; prepare substantive briefs on possible areas of cooperation. Lead the design of Ending Violence against Women initiatives in the region and the development of relevant knowledge products Lead the provision of policy recommendations and guidance to strategic planning and positioning on Ending Violence against Women; Lead and provide advice to regional/ national bodies; represent UN Women in interagency groups that influence national policies related to Ending Violence against Women Contribute substantively and lead existing thematic and gender equality networks to better connect UN Women and partners; Lead the research, development, and presentation of analytical reports, research papers, briefing notes, background papers, summaries, correspondence on Ending Violence against Women Identify promising practices, technical expertise, and strategic opportunities. Manage knowledge building and sharing for Ending Violence against Women Identify and disseminate lessons learnt and good practices in collaboration with country offices; Ensure technical skills and knowledge are shared within and among CO Manage and monitor the regional knowledge platform and innovative approaches in Ending Violence against Women The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization. Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: The incumbent leads a team of 4 personnel, including 1 P-3, 1G6 and 2 NPSA all under direct report. Competencies : Core Values: Integrity; Professionalism; Respect for Diversity. Core Competencies: Awareness and Sensitivity Regarding Gender Issues; Accountability; Creative Problem Solving; Effective Communication; Inclusive Collaboration; Stakeholder Engagement; Leading by Example. Please visit this link for more information on UN Women’s Values and Competencies Framework: Functional Competencies: Excellent knowledge of Ending Violence against Women Strong knowledge of region Excellent networking skills Ability to interact with donors, identify and analyze trends, opportunities, and threats to fundraising. Ability to perform qualitative and quantitative policy research Ability to advocate and provide policy advice Excellent analytical skills Ability to write policy papers, speeches, briefings Excellent knowledge of programme development, implementation, results-based management and reporting Recruitment Qualifications: Education and certification: Master’s degree or equivalent in gender, human rights, international relations or other social science fields is required. A first-level university degree in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Experience: At least 7 years progressively responsible experience in designing and managing programmes and advocating for Ending Violence against Women ideally with some experience in developing countries is required. Experience in programme, policy analysis, and strategic planning is required. Experience working with, and building partnerships with governments, donors and civil society organizations internationally and in the field is required Experience working with the UN system is desirable. Experience working in West and Central Africa is desirable. Language Requirements: Fluency in English and French is required. Knowledge of another official UN language is desirable (French, Arabic, Chinese, Russian or Spanish). Statements : In July 2010, the United Nations General Assembly created UN Women, the United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women. The creation of UN Women came about as part of the UN reform agenda, bringing together resources and mandates for greater impact. It merges and builds on the important work of four previously distinct parts of the UN system (DAW, OSAGI, INSTRAW and UNIFEM), which focused exclusively on gender equality and women's empowerment. UN Women recruits, employs, trains, compensates, and promotes regardless of race, religion, color, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, ability, national origin, or any other basis covered by appropriate law. All employment is decided on the basis of qualifications, competence, integrity and organizational need. If you need any reasonable accommodation to support your participation in the recruitment and selection process, please include this information in your application. UN Women has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UN Women, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination. All selected candidates will be expected to adhere to UN Women’s policies and procedures,, and the standards of conduct expected of UN Women personnel and will therefore undergo rigorous reference and background checks. (Background checks will include the verification of academic credential(s) and employment history. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information to conduct a background check.) review_candidates.title: Business Support System Specialist
review_candidates.description: Technology You Will Work With: Large language models consumed through APIs (Alibaba Qwen / Model Studio, Anthropic Claude, OpenAI and comparable providers). Prompt engineering, system instructions, structured (JSON) outputs and tool / function calling. Retrieval-augmented generation: embeddings, chunking and vector search. Speech-to-text, text-to-speech and image and document recognition (OCR) services. Python or TypeScript for the scripts, integrations and evaluations you write. Evaluation, prompt versioning and observability tooling, with Git and GitHub for review and history. Key Responsibilities: Design, write and iterate on the prompts and system instructions that drive the product's AI assistant, and version them the way code is versioned. Turn business rules and operating procedures into instructions, examples and constraints that a model follows reliably. Define and maintain the assistant's tools — what each one does, the arguments it takes and when the model should reach for it — working with engineers on the implementation. Prepare the knowledge the assistant reads: collect, clean, chunk and structure source material, and keep it current as the business changes. Build evaluation sets for every AI feature, run them on each change, and report accuracy, regressions and failure patterns with evidence rather than impressions. Integrate and tune speech recognition and image or document recognition so they hold up on real user input, including accented speech and poor-quality photographs. Investigate reported AI failures — a wrong answer, an invented fact, a missed or mis-called tool — and trace each one to its cause in the prompt, the retrieved data or the tool definition. Monitor token usage, latency and cost per request, and propose changes that reduce them without weakening quality. Test the assistant across the languages it serves and confirm it answers correctly in each of them. Apply responsible-use practice: keep sensitive data out of prompts and logs, and flag outputs that should never be produced. Write clear documentation of what the assistant can and cannot do, and update the in-app user manual whenever your change alters what a user sees or gets. Requirements: Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Engineering, or a related field. 1–3 years of experience building with large language models or other AI services. Internships and substantial personal or open-source AI projects will be considered. Demonstrable prompt engineering experience with a commercial LLM, and the judgement to explain why one prompt outperforms another. Working understanding of how these models behave: tokens and context windows, temperature, embeddings, structured output, and the common causes of hallucination. Comfortable reading and writing code to call APIs and process JSON — Python or JavaScript / TypeScript is sufficient; you do not need to be a full-stack engineer. Able to design test cases and evaluate model output objectively against them. Familiarity with structured data: JSON, CSV and basic SQL. Comfortable with Git and a pull-request based workflow. Strong analytical, problem-solving and communication skills, with attention to detail. Excellent command of written and spoken English.

review_candidates.title: Data Engineer
review_candidates.description: Data Engineer with Significant Impact Are you a skilled data engineer able to translate raw data to decision-ready analyses, and want to make a difference in a strong, Nordic media company with a European footprint? Story House Egmont is looking for a Data Engineer for our European technology department. We deliver great data and processes to support decisions throughout Europe. What you will be doing You’ll be a part of a small but important Data and AI team working with the media business of Story House Egmont. You’ll work closely with departments across Europe such as the Nordic marketing department, which depends on our data for their subscription business. A large amount of our work is within the Nordics, but also England with, Poland and Germany. For this position we’re looking for someone with approximately 2-5 years experience, who enjoys autonomy, responsibility and the ability to impact how we work. You don’t need to be familiar with our entire tech stack before you begin, but you must have a technical background from either work or education. You should enjoy complex challenges and be able to balance the desire for a technically elegant solution with the need to be pragmatic. It’s beneficial if you have a good understanding of business or want to learn more. You’ll be able to contribute to AI-related projects according to your own interest and capacity. Several projects have a data and an AI element, but many are also separate. Our tech stack We work with dbt models, orchestrated through Dagster, which we self-host in Kubernetes. Our data lake is in GCS. The data warehouse is in BigQuery, and we deliver reports in Power BI. Some information is also delivered through large language models. An important part of the job is including new data sources, API or file-based, into our Dagster flow. We also work on some machine learning models. You should have experience with: SQL and practical data warehouse work Python Machine learning Integrating new data sources and imports (ETL/ELT) Power BI or similar We hope you have experience with some of this: dbt Dagster BigQuery Kubernetes (we work in k8s, but it’s ran centrally) GitHub We offer: A varied workday in a fast-paced work environment Great work environment and skilled colleagues Social activities and/or clubs depending on the country, company cabins/summer house, and more! An important role in a renowned media company This is a permanent position in the team Data & AI, and reports to Data & AI Manager Henrik Hildre. The team is a part of a European technology department with teams working on content systems, web development, data and subscription systems. Our head office is in Copenhagen, and the technology department has employees in Oslo, Stockholm, Malmö, København and Warszawa. We believe data engineers from all backgrounds will feel welcome with us! The working language is Norwegian, Swedish or Danish. You’ll have some meetings in English too. For this position we’re hiring in Norway, Sweden and Denmark. You’ll be formally hired in the country you’re in, with local terms and a base in the relevant office (Oslo, Malmö, Copenhagen). Application deadline is September 30th 2026. We’ll have interviews on a rolling basis and could make quick decisions for the right candidate. We don’t work with recruitment companies, please apply personally. Regarding AI applications: This job description was not written with AI, and we have no AI systems automatically screening applications or CVs. All applications are read and considered by the head of the team. To make it easier to separate your opinions from that of an AI agent, please don’t write a long and complex application with your AI assistant. We’d love to see a human paragraph or two about what you think is interesting about the position, why you’re applying and what you can contribute with at Story House Egmont. We’re looking for a great data engineer, not perfect language. Should you have any questions regarding the position, please do not hesitate to contact: Henrik Hildre, Manager Data & AI, henrik.hildre@egmont.com. Please click “Apply” to apply – we do not accept applications via email. About Story House Egmont Story House Egmont publishes magazines, comics, books, and digital services for adults, children, and young people. We are also a co-owner of several successful companies within e-commerce and marketing services. Our motto – We bring stories to life – is rooted in strong publishing values. We create great content and world-class journalism, and develop engaging consumer communities and brands. Story House is part of Egmont, one of the leading media groups in the Nordic region. Egmont is behind TV 2, Nordisk Film, Cappelen Damm, and Lindhardt og Ringhof in Denmark. Egmont is a foundation where all profits are reinvested into developing our companies, helping vulnerable children and youth, and supporting film talent. We are passionate about creating everyday magic, both for our customers and in our day-to-day work life. Here, you will meet dedicated, positive, and adaptable colleagues who care about one another and work together toward a shared goal. We believe in the value of our differences and diverse perspectives. It is through diversity and varied viewpoints that great stories are born. We therefore warmly welcome diversity.

Build valuable skills in troubleshooting, automation, documentation, and cross-team collaboration. new_matches.title: Network Administrator
new_matches.description: Network Administrator RJ45, SFP+, QSFP, IP, BGP, TCP, UDP, TLS, DHCP, SFTP, F5... Pokud to pro tebe není jen shluk náhodných znaků, ale vidíš za tím živou infrastrukturu, zbystři. Hledáme parťáka, který má síťařinu v krvi, rád řeší komplexní technické výzvy a chce rozšířit tým lidí, kteří IT doslova žijí. Tato pozice není o rutinním klikání – naše síť je živý, různorodý organismus plný moderních technologií a její správa vyžaduje maximální zodpovědnost. Co budeš dělat? Komplexní správa a rozvoj: Kompletní péče o naši síťovou infrastrukturu od návrhu až po realizaci. Architektura a inovace: Nebudeš jen udržovat status quo – čeká tě implementace nových technologií a aktivní vyhledávání cest k optimalizaci a modernizaci sítě. Instalace a konfigurace: Hardwaru i softwaru (u nás si sáhneš na spoustu různých technologií). Troubleshooting: Diagnostika a řešení složitých síťových incidentů, které vyžadují analytické myšlení a rychlé jednání. Podpora: Řešení pokročilých požadavků od našich zákazníků i kolegů. Co od tebe očekáváme? Vysokou míru zodpovědnosti a pečlivosti: Výpadky sítě bolí. Hledáme člověka, který domýšlí věci do důsledku, nezkracuje si cestu a na jehož práci je 100% spolehnutí. Zápal a chuť se samovzdělávat: Technologie letí dopředu a náš stack je pestrý. Klíčový je pro nás tvůj vnitřní drive – musíš se chtít učit nové věci sám od sebe, sledovat trendy a neustále se v oboru rozvíjet. Solidní základ: Znalosti v oblasti správy sítí, routovacích/switchingových protokolů a základní administraci OS Linux. Vzdělání: VŠ nebo SŠ technického zaměření (CISCO akademie je velkou výhodou). Komunikativnost a týmovost: Nebát se mluvit se zákazníkem i kolegy, umět věci vysvětlit, ptát se. Flexibilitu: Občasné držení pohotovosti (L2, střídáme se fér v rámci týmu). Co u nás získáš? Zázemí stabilní, ryze české společnosti s dlouholetou historií. Pružnou pracovní dobu: Fixní čas máme od 9:00 do 15:00, zbytek si plánuješ podle sebe. 5 týdnů dovolené. Finanční ohodnocení, které odpovídá náročnosti pozice + podílové odměny. Uvolněnou a přátelskou atmosféru. Všichni si tykáme, pomáháme si a chápeme, že každý má někdy den blbec.

new_matches.title: Information and Communications Technology (ICT) Officer (P)
new_matches.description: Job Description Introduction Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental, and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants. IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive, and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration . Applications are welcome from first- and second-tier candidates, particularly qualified female candidates as well as applications from the non-represented member countries of IOM. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, the following are considered first-tier candidates: Internal candidates Candidates from the following IOM Member States that are not represented among staff members in the Professional and higher categories: Bahamas, Barbados, Cabo Verde, Comoros, Congo (the), Cook Islands, Dominica, Federated States of Micronesia, Grenada, Guinea-Bissau, Holy See, Iceland, Israel, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Namibia, Nauru, Palau, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Samoa, Sao Tome and Principe, Seychelles, Solomon Islands, Suriname, Timor-Leste, Tonga, Trinidad and Tobago, Tuvalu, Vanuatu Second Tier Candidates Include All external candidates, except candidates from non-represented member states of IOM. Organizational Context and Scope Under the overall supervision of Chief of Mission (CoM), direct supervision of the Head of Resources Management and in close coordination with relevant staff from ICT department counterparts in the Regional Officer Asia and Pacific (ROAP) and the Department of Information and Communications Technology at HQ, the Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Officer will supervise and coordinate the ICT operations in the Country Office (CO) including its Sub-Offices. Responsibilities Supervise and coordinate the activities of the Information and Communications Technology (ICT) Unit in the Country Office by ensuring that all requirements are addressed in a timely and accurately, with an efficient allocation of resources, and that all operations are in compliance with IOM ICT policies and standards and are in line with the ICT strategy. Coordinate the continuous engagement and liaison with the CO’s management, Heads of units and field operations, for the adequate and timely provision of ICT solutions and services to satisfy operational needs, including emergencies as necessary. Act as the ICT business relationship and cybersecurity local liaison Focal Point with counterparts such as IOM programmes, global cybersecurity programme, Governmental, donors, United Nations Agencies, Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs), ICT service providers, and Vendors for coordinated and adequate provision of ICT services, digital innovation, technologies and supplies. Participate in the ICT Working Group in the country, representing the CO in discussions and initiatives. Provide technical support for the CO’s ICT services and supervise, train, and equip the CO’s ICT Team to effectively implement strategic initiatives, timely respond to information security incidents, and provide Tier 1 support and escalate to the relevant specialist teams/units, when needed, for immediate corrective/remedial actions. Contribute to the preparation of the CO’s ICT documentation including office-specific Standard Operating Procedures (SOP), Business Continuity Plan, Disaster Recovery Plans and ICT Risk record for the CO’s ICT-related services. Coordinate and monitor the delivery and efficiency of services and redundancy in line with IOM ICT standards while checking that global ICT SOPs are complied with. Contribute to the service improvement assessments and provide recommendations to the CO’s management to optimize and implement ICT Infrastructure and solutions to ensure the efficient functioning of CO’s operations. Maintain and check that all technical specifications for procurement and provision of ICT-related equipment, supplies, services, and technical evaluations are in line with ICT standards and policies, and are adequately managed. Liaise with CO’s Supply Chain Unit to guide on proper provision of ICT-related equipment, supplies, services, and propose the most suitable solutions. In coordination with the ICT Information Security Unit at HQ, act as the Focal Point, the first line of cybersecurity defense, and first local cybersecurity incident responder in the CO. Facilitate the implementation of security and compliance controls of the IOM global cybersecurity programme and compliance with the IOM global cybersecurity, and other compliances required by the donors, operational frameworks and standards. Perform such other duties as may be assigned. Qualifications Required Qualifications and Experience Education Master’s degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Information Management, Information Technology, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with two years of relevant professional experience; or, University degree in the above fields with four years of relevant professional experience. Certificate in any of the following: Cisco Certified Network Associate (CCNA), Microsoft Azure certifications, Microsoft Certified System Administrator (MCSA), Microsoft Certified Database Administrator (MCDBA), Microsoft Certified System Engineer (MCSE) is a distinct advantage. Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database. Experience Experience in overseeing and managing the implementation and administration of Microsoft Windows and serverless network environments (LAN/WAN) and first-level network/desktop support in a large international organization is required; Experience in a supervisory role and management of ICT functions in an international organization or an international agency in a field location; supporting emergency, complex/post-conflict Country Office; Experience in planning, design, development, implementation, and maintenance of computer information systems; Knowledge and demonstrated experience in cybersecurity compliance and security implementation and maintenance, database information systems, and data processing tools. Knowledge of web-based development and other development tools and reporting, including future projections on the potential of current and new technologies; Good knowledge and experience in Microsoft 365 cloud-based applications and technologies; and, Experience providing policy advice to senior managers on systems development in a changing business environment and the implications of various alternatives, on business applications planned for future needs and other related issues. Skills Good oral and written communication skills; refined soft skills and demonstrated ability to communicate with business leaders and those with limited technical background effectively is essential; Good knowledge of Windows Operating System, Network\Systems administration, TCP/IP, Telecoms, Network Protocols, Cisco devices, VPN, VoIP, MS Office 365 apps, Antivirus Software, and utilities; Good knowledge of web-based development, geographical information systems, and/or mapping tools would be a distinctive advantage; Demonstrated ability to work with minimal supervision and demonstrate a high level of initiative, perseverance, and professional commitment to achieve high-quality results; Demonstrated ability to handle confidential data in a professional, responsible, and mature manner; and, Demonstrated ability to train individuals, to work effectively and harmoniously with colleagues within a team from varied cultures and professional backgrounds. Languages For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written). Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage. Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments. Required Competencies IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link . Competencies will be assessed during the selection process. Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values: Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion. Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct. Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges. Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance. Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated. Core Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2 Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results. Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action-oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes. Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate. Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work. Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way. Managerial Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2 Leadership: Provides a clear sense of direction, leads by example and demonstrates the ability to carry out the Organization’s vision. Assists others to realize and develop their leadership and professional potential. Empowering others: Creates an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential. Building Trust: Promotes shared values and creates an atmosphere of trust and honesty. Strategic thinking and vision: Works strategically to realize the Organization’s goals and communicates a clear strategic direction. Humility: Leads with humility and shows openness to acknowledging own shortcomings. Notes Internationally recruited professional staff are required to be mobile. Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category. Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation. This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months. Appointment will be subject to all clearances, including medical and security, as well as accreditation, and any residency or visa requirements. Vacancies close at 23:59 local time in Geneva, Switzerland on the respective closing date. No late applications will be accepted. new_matches.title: Solutions Architect for Automotive
new_matches.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Solutions Architect for Automotive based in United Arab Emirates. This is a high-impact technical role focused on helping automotive organizations adopt innovative open-source technologies and build the next generation of software-defined vehicles. You will combine automotive expertise with strong Linux, embedded systems, and software development knowledge to solve complex customer challenges. The role spans presales consulting, technical solution design, demonstrations, proof-of-concepts, and selected project delivery. You will collaborate with specialists across cloud, Kubernetes, security, safety, and embedded technologies to develop comprehensive solutions for customers and partners. Your work will help shape market requirements and influence the evolution of technologies supporting connected, intelligent, and software-defined automotive platforms. The position offers exposure to ambitious technology organizations and diverse engagements across the rapidly evolving automotive and open-source ecosystem. This opportunity is well suited to a customer-focused technologist who enjoys solving complex problems, learning quickly, and turning emerging technologies into practical business outcomes. Accountabilities Engage with automotive customers during presales activities to understand requirements, identify challenges, and explain relevant technologies and solutions. Act as a trusted technical advisor and customer advocate, helping organizations evaluate and adopt open-source platforms for automotive use cases. Collaborate with specialists in cloud, Kubernetes, security, safety, embedded systems, and other technical domains to develop comprehensive customer solutions. Participate in selected Embedded Linux projects, including technical demonstrations, prototypes, and proof-of-concepts. Translate customer and market requirements into actionable insights for internal engineering, product, and business stakeholders. Contribute to the development and refinement of reusable technical solutions that address emerging automotive market opportunities. Support initiatives related to software-defined vehicles and the application of cloud technologies to embedded automotive environments. Communicate complex technical concepts clearly to both technical and business audiences through presentations, demonstrations, and customer discussions. Balance multiple customer engagements and priorities while maintaining a strong focus on delivery, quality, and business outcomes. Requirements Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Relevant professional experience within the automotive industry. Extensive Linux experience, with strong knowledge of Debian or Ubuntu preferred. Solid Embedded Linux experience, including exposure to Yocto and/or real-time operating systems. Strong programming or scripting skills in one or more of Golang, Python, C, C++, or Rust. Understanding of low-level Linux boot processes, BIOS, firmware, and embedded software development methodologies. Professional written and spoken English combined with proficiency in the local language. Excellent communication, presentation, and customer-facing skills. Ability to understand customer environments, identify needs, pitch solutions, and deliver technical demonstrations. Strong problem-solving skills with a results-oriented approach and the ability to manage multiple priorities. Self-motivated, accountable, adaptable, and committed to delivering on agreed objectives. Curious, humble, and eager to learn new technologies and apply them to evolving automotive challenges. Experience with ISO 26262 and/or ISO 21434 is a plus. Previous experience in customer-facing technical engagements is an advantage. Willingness and ability to travel up to approximately 30% for customer meetings, company events, conferences, and other professional engagements. Benefits Competitive compensation based on geographical location, experience, and performance. Performance-driven annual bonus. Annual compensation reviews. Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year. Recognition and performance rewards. Annual holiday leave. Maternity and paternity leave. Employee Assistance Programme. Distributed working environment with opportunities to meet colleagues in person during team events and technical sprints. Opportunities to travel internationally for customer engagements, conferences, and team events. Priority Pass and travel upgrades for eligible long-haul company events. Exposure to cutting-edge open-source, Linux, cloud, embedded, and automotive technologies. Opportunity to contribute to the development of software-defined vehicle technologies and emerging automotive platforms. Collaboration with globally distributed engineering teams and specialists across multiple technical disciplines. How Jobgether Works We use an AI-powered matching process to ensure your application is reviewed quickly, objectively, and fairly against the role's core requirements. Our system identifies the top-fitting candidates, and this shortlist is then shared directly with the hiring company. The final decision and next steps (interviews, assessments) are managed by their internal team. We appreciate your interest and wish you the best! Why Apply Through Jobgether? Data Privacy Notice: By submitting your application, you acknowledge that Jobgether will process your personal data to evaluate your candidacy and share relevant information with the hiring employer. This processing is based on legitimate interest and pre-contractual measures under applicable data protection laws (including GDPR). You may exercise your rights (access, rectification, erasure, objection) at any time. We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace, and security.
