The FPI envisions a multi-year and multi-country programme of work, complemented by global and regional strategies linking normative and technical work on gender statistics at the global level to the regional and national levels through three interlinked areas of work: Building a supportive policy and institutional environment for the localization and effective monitoring of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs); Increasing the quality, comparability, and regularity of gender statistics to address national data gaps and meet reporting commitments under the SDGs; and Ensuring that gender statistics are accessible to users in governments, civil society, academia, and the private sector, to strengthen adequate demand for their production. In line with this global FPI developed by UN Women HQ, UN Women Arab States Regional Office developed a regional project that is specific to the context of the Arab States region and responds to the Regional Strategic Note 2026-29 in order to: Advance the production and use of gender statistics across the region and strengthen national-level SDGs monitoring and reporting through building holistic systems at national and regional level to measure SDG 5 and other key SDG indicators that require sex-disaggregation; and Collaborate with regional bodies/partners in the Arab States to produce comprehensive and comparative gender statistics, analysis and advance accessibility and knowledge sharing. new_matches.title: Head of Programme Coordination and Innovation Unit (P)
new_matches.description: Job Description Introduction Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental, and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants. IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive, and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration . Applications are welcome from first- and second-tier candidates, particularly qualified female candidates as well as applications from the non-represented member countries of IOM. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, the following are considered first-tier candidates: Internal candidates Candidates from the following IOM Member States that are not represented among staff members in the Professional and higher categories: Bahamas, Barbados, Cabo Verde, Comoros, Congo (the), Cook Islands, Dominica, Federated States of Micronesia, Grenada, Guinea-Bissau, Holy See, Iceland, Israel, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Namibia, Nauru, Palau, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Samoa, Sao Tome and Principe, Seychelles, Solomon Islands, Suriname, Timor-Leste, Tonga, Trinidad and Tobago, Tuvalu, Vanuatu Second Tier Candidates Include All external candidates, except candidates from non-represented member states of IOM. Organizational Context and Scope Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission (CoM) and direct supervision of the Deputy Chief of Mission (DCoM), in coordination with the Programme Managers, Senior Resource Management Officer, Heads of Sub-Offices IOM West and Central of Africa Regional Office (RO) and IOM’s Headquarters (HQ), the Head of Programme Coordination and Innovation Unit (PCIU) will be responsible for the management and coordination of unit activities, including programme and project conceptualization, proposal development, Monitoring and Evaluation, support the Country Office (CO) strategic planning and relationships with UN, donors and the Government of Nigeria, particularly in relation to the operational aspects of programmes/projects and resource mobilization. Responsibilities Manage and supervise the staff of the Mission Support and Innovation Unit, ensuring their effective and timely performance of development, implementation, and reporting tasks for IOM Nigeria’s programmes/projects according to institutional guidance. Assess potential project and funding opportunities, prepare project proposals and concept notes in the areas of interest to IOM Nigeria, and review and improve project reports, fact sheets and other documents in coordination with relevant Programme/Project managers and programme units. Support the coordination and evaluation of programme and project activities of IOM Nigeria to ensure timely and effective implementation and quality reporting and advise the DCoM of the corrective measures that may be needed. Support liaison with donors, project partners, other IOM Country Offices, RO, and HQ to facilitate coordinated project implementation and synergies and to make recommendations on donor/partner engagement. Provide advice for the mainstreaming of relevant African Union, Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), West African Community, Intergovernmental Authority on Development and Common Market for West Africa policies and frameworks into internal frameworks, policies, as well as national-level programming and design. Keep abreast of and analyse migration issues, policies, and emerging trends, identify priorities, and recommend actions to the Deputy Chief of Mission in relation to risks and opportunities for IOM. Identify priorities, challenges and issues to be addressed within the country office as appropriate and propose corrective actions. Provide support and guidance to Programme/Project Managers and other project staff on programme/project implementation, monitoring and evaluation, and quality assurance. Participate in relevant UN and inter-agency meetings and mechanisms to facilitate the integration of IOM programmes into inter-agency processes and the mainstreaming of migration into Common Country Analysis and Cooperation frameworks. Support IOM Nigeria in working with respective national counterparts to facilitate cooperation, external relations, and liaison activities. In close coordination with the Information Management System Officer, provide evidence-based information on IOM Nigeria’s project development and fundraising efforts through targeted assessment surveys, analyses, studies, and systematic publication. Develop and disseminate communications and visibility materials, such as quarterly reports, newsletters, flash reports, etc., and respond to information requests from HQ and Regional Office. Facilitate the generation and use of knowledge to promote improved policy engagement, project development and management in Nigeria and the West and Central Africa region. Perform such other duties as may be assigned. Qualifications Required Qualifications and Experience Education Master’s degree in Political or Social Science, International Relations, Law, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with five years of relevant professional experience; or, University degree in the above fields with seven years of relevant professional experience. Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database. Experience Experience in the field of international migration, management, and evaluation; Work experience in the field of migration issues, including operational and field experience, IOM Project Development, Management, Implementation and Monitoring systems; Experience in dealing with donors on project implementation and reporting; Experience and excellent understanding of the migration themes in West Africa and extensive knowledge of the arid and semi-arid regions; and, Experience in liaising with governmental authorities, other national/international institutions, and Non-Governmental Organizations. Skills Knowledge in project monitoring and evaluation is required; Demonstrated expertise in thematic areas relevant to project liaison, reporting, and monitoring; and, Knowledge and experience of regional issues is an advantage. Languages For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written). Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage. Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments. Required Competencies IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link . Competencies will be assessed during the selection process. Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values: Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion. Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct. Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges. Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance. Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated. Core Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2 Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results. Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action-oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes. Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate. Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work. Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way. Managerial Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2 Leadership: Provides a clear sense of direction, leads by example and demonstrates the ability to carry out the Organization’s vision. Assists others to realize and develop their leadership and professional potential. Empowering others: Creates an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential. Building Trust: Promotes shared values and creates an atmosphere of trust and honesty. Strategic thinking and vision: Works strategically to realize the Organization’s goals and communicates a clear strategic direction. Humility: Leads with humility and shows openness to acknowledging own shortcomings. Notes Internationally recruited professional staff are required to be mobile. Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category. Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation. This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months. Appointment will be subject to all clearances, including medical and security, as well as accreditation, and any residency or visa requirements. Vacancies close at 23:59 local time in Geneva, Switzerland, on the respective closing date. No late applications will be accepted. IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, harassment, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and any forms of discrimination. IOM is committed to promote the protection and safeguarding of all children. IOM conducts reference checks and background verification, including through system-wide databases such as ClearCheck, to help ensure that candidates have no record of misconduct, including on sexual harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, or fraud. Candidates are expected to uphold these standards and principles at all times. IOM does not charge any fees at any stage of the recruitment process—whether for application, interview, processing, training, or otherwise—and does not request any information related to bank accounts. IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM WAVE system (for internal candidates, link here ). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies.

Establish machine-specific maintenance schedules and ensure timely execution. Ensure availability and reliability of confectionery processing and packaging equipment . Ensure maintenance activities comply with engineering, food safety, and GMP standards. Provide technical support to production teams during breakdowns, start-ups, and changeovers. 2. Reliability and Equipment Performance Key Responsibilities Monitor and analyze machine breakdowns and equipment failures. Lead Root Cause Analysis (RCA) investigations and implement corrective and preventive actions. Track and improve MTBF and MTTR. Develop reliability-centered maintenance programs for critical confectionery equipment. Implement condition-monitoring techniques. Identify recurring equipment failures and develop long-term engineering solutions. Analyze equipment-related production losses and recommend improvement initiatives. Improve the reliability of critical processing and packaging assets. Relevant Equipment May Include Chocolate processing and tempering equipment. Chocolate moulding and depositing machines. Enrobing machines. Candy and toffee cooking systems. Batch and continuous cooking systems. Mixing and kneading equipment. Biscuit/wafer processing equipment, where applicable. Cooling tunnels and refrigeration systems. Conveyors and material handling systems. Wrapping, flow-pack, cartoning and secondary packaging machines. Metal detectors, checkweighers and coding equipment. Outcomes Improved equipment reliability. Reduced unplanned downtime. Improved MTBF and reduced MTTR. Reduction in recurring equipment failures. Improved OEE of critical production lines. 3. Utilities Management Key Responsibilities Manage all plant utilities required for confectionery manufacturing, including: Water treatment systems. Boilers and steam systems. Air compressors. Refrigeration systems. Chillers and cooling systems. HVAC and air-handling systems. Power distribution systems. Wastewater treatment facilities. Ensure uninterrupted utility services to support production requirements. Monitor utility consumption and identify opportunities for optimization. Ensure utility systems comply with safety, environmental, food safety, and regulatory requirements. Develop preventive and predictive maintenance programs for utility equipment. Improved water, electricity, steam, compressed-air and refrigeration efficiency. Reduced energy consumption per unit of production. Engineering Budget and Cost Management Key Responsibilities Prepare and manage the Engineering and Maintenance budget. Monitor maintenance expenditure against approved budgets. Identify opportunities to reduce maintenance and utility costs. Evaluate repair-versus-replacement decisions. Develop technical and financial justifications for CAPEX proposals. Monitor contractor and service-provider costs. Outcomes Maintenance spending controlled within budget. Cost savings through improved equipment reliability and energy efficiency. Investment decisions supported by clear technical and operational justification. 6. Engineering Projects and Capital Expenditure Key Responsibilities Plan, coordinate and implement engineering projects. Coordinate contractors, OEMs and service providers. Lead commissioning and performance verification of new equipment. Support line automation, modernization and capacity expansion projects. Team Leadership & Capability Development Lead, coach and develop the Engineering and Maintenance team. Develop and maintain an Engineering Skill Matrix. new_matches.title: Data Engineer
new_matches.description: Data Engineer with Significant Impact Are you a skilled data engineer able to translate raw data to decision-ready analyses, and want to make a difference in a strong, Nordic media company with a European footprint? Story House Egmont is looking for a Data Engineer for our European technology department. We deliver great data and processes to support decisions throughout Europe. What you will be doing You’ll be a part of a small but important Data and AI team working with the media business of Story House Egmont. You’ll work closely with departments across Europe such as the Nordic marketing department, which depends on our data for their subscription business. A large amount of our work is within the Nordics, but also England with, Poland and Germany. For this position we’re looking for someone with approximately 2-5 years experience, who enjoys autonomy, responsibility and the ability to impact how we work. You don’t need to be familiar with our entire tech stack before you begin, but you must have a technical background from either work or education. You should enjoy complex challenges and be able to balance the desire for a technically elegant solution with the need to be pragmatic. It’s beneficial if you have a good understanding of business or want to learn more. You’ll be able to contribute to AI-related projects according to your own interest and capacity. Several projects have a data and an AI element, but many are also separate. Our tech stack We work with dbt models, orchestrated through Dagster, which we self-host in Kubernetes. Our data lake is in GCS. The data warehouse is in BigQuery, and we deliver reports in Power BI. Some information is also delivered through large language models. An important part of the job is including new data sources, API or file-based, into our Dagster flow. We also work on some machine learning models. You should have experience with: SQL and practical data warehouse work Python Machine learning Integrating new data sources and imports (ETL/ELT) Power BI or similar We hope you have experience with some of this: dbt Dagster BigQuery Kubernetes (we work in k8s, but it’s ran centrally) GitHub We offer: A varied workday in a fast-paced work environment Great work environment and skilled colleagues Social activities and/or clubs depending on the country, company cabins/summer house, and more! An important role in a renowned media company This is a permanent position in the team Data & AI, and reports to Data & AI Manager Henrik Hildre. The team is a part of a European technology department with teams working on content systems, web development, data and subscription systems. Our head office is in Copenhagen, and the technology department has employees in Oslo, Stockholm, Malmö, København and Warszawa. We believe data engineers from all backgrounds will feel welcome with us! The working language is Norwegian, Swedish or Danish. You’ll have some meetings in English too. For this position we’re hiring in Norway, Sweden and Denmark. You’ll be formally hired in the country you’re in, with local terms and a base in the relevant office (Oslo, Malmö, Copenhagen). Application deadline is September 30th 2026. We’ll have interviews on a rolling basis and could make quick decisions for the right candidate. We don’t work with recruitment companies, please apply personally. Regarding AI applications: This job description was not written with AI, and we have no AI systems automatically screening applications or CVs. All applications are read and considered by the head of the team. To make it easier to separate your opinions from that of an AI agent, please don’t write a long and complex application with your AI assistant. We’d love to see a human paragraph or two about what you think is interesting about the position, why you’re applying and what you can contribute with at Story House Egmont. We’re looking for a great data engineer, not perfect language. Should you have any questions regarding the position, please do not hesitate to contact: Henrik Hildre, Manager Data & AI, henrik.hildre@egmont.com. Please click “Apply” to apply – we do not accept applications via email. About Story House Egmont Story House Egmont publishes magazines, comics, books, and digital services for adults, children, and young people. We are also a co-owner of several successful companies within e-commerce and marketing services. Our motto – We bring stories to life – is rooted in strong publishing values. We create great content and world-class journalism, and develop engaging consumer communities and brands. Story House is part of Egmont, one of the leading media groups in the Nordic region. Egmont is behind TV 2, Nordisk Film, Cappelen Damm, and Lindhardt og Ringhof in Denmark. Egmont is a foundation where all profits are reinvested into developing our companies, helping vulnerable children and youth, and supporting film talent. We are passionate about creating everyday magic, both for our customers and in our day-to-day work life. Here, you will meet dedicated, positive, and adaptable colleagues who care about one another and work together toward a shared goal. We believe in the value of our differences and diverse perspectives. It is through diversity and varied viewpoints that great stories are born. We therefore warmly welcome diversity.

We are committed to embracing new state-of-the-art technologies and advancements, propelling us towards a cleaner, brighter tomorrow. Our positive footprint extends across five continents, creating a lasting impact. At METLEN, we foster a culture of resilience, challenge, respect, excellence, and change , empowering our diverse workforce to achieve remarkable outcomes. We are currently looking for a Backend Developer to join Joule our new energy software company, part of our Integrated Energy Utility Division , based in Paiania. This opportunity is ideal for a software professional looking to contribute to the development of scalable digital solutions supporting energy services, data-driven applications, and smart energy systems. Your Role Will Encompass: Designing, developing, and maintaining scalable backend services and APIs using Python, Django and/or Flask. Working with PostgreSQL and MongoDB for data storage and processing. Developing data-driven solutions using Pandas and NumPy. Containerizing applications using Docker and collaborating through Git. Troubleshooting and optimizing backend applications in distributed and data-intensive environments. Collaborating with frontend developers, data scientists, and energy domain experts to deliver new features and solutions. What You Bring to the Role: 3+ years of professional backend development experience. Strong proficiency in Python and hands-on experience with Django and/or Flask. Solid knowledge of PostgreSQL and MongoDB. Familiarity with Docker, Git, Pandas and NumPy. Strong debugging, problem-solving, and performance-tuning skills. Experience with Golang and Gin, time-series data, or networking concepts will be considered an asset. Familiarity with Modbus, MQTT, OPC UA, or IEC 60870-5-104 (IEC104) will be considered an asset. Interest or previous experience in energy, smart grids, renewable energy, or industrial IoT will be considered an asset. Share the same Value Based Behaviors: People & Personal growth. Results orientation & Safety excellence. Collaboration & Trust. Empathy & Effective communication. Flexibility & Adaptability. Your Benefits: Competitive remuneration package. Ticket Restaurant. Follow us on LinkedIn and stay updated on our latest news We respect your personal data. All personal information in your application and CV will remain strictly confidential.
